scenarioStory.history: Wife reports three days of productive cough with yellow-green sputum and fever, worsening over the last 24 hours. This morning he became increasingly short of breath and confused, prompting the 911 call.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 71-year-old male with three days of worsening productive cough and fever, now hypoxic, tachypneic, confused, and hypotensive, consistent with severe sepsis from a pulmonary source. → O2 and IV fluids started: Crew begins supplemental oxygen and IV fluid resuscitation for suspected septic shock from a pulmonary source, sequencing fluids before adding positive-pressure support given the patient's hypotension. → Fluid-refractory shock, norepinephrine started: With persistent hypotension despite fluids, the crew starts norepinephrine and carefully adds CPAP for the ongoing hypoxia, watching closely for any hemodynamic effect from the added intrathoracic pressure. → Perfusion and oxygenation improve, transport continues: With combined fluid, pressor, and respiratory support, the patient's perfusion and oxygenation trend toward normal. The crew continues serial reassessment and maintains the CPAP seal throughout transport.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 71-year-old male with three days of worsening productive cough and fever, now hypoxic, tachypneic, confused, and hypotensive, consistent with severe sepsis from a pulmonary source.

scenarioEvents.name: O2 and IV fluids started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew begins supplemental oxygen and IV fluid resuscitation for suspected septic shock from a pulmonary source, sequencing fluids before adding positive-pressure support given the patient's hypotension.
relatedChecklist: Administer supplemental oxygen via non-rebreather targeting SpO2 94-98%
Establish IV access; begin 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus, pressure infused over less than 15 min toward MAP 65 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid-refractory shock, norepinephrine started
scenarioEvents.description: With persistent hypotension despite fluids, the crew starts norepinephrine and carefully adds CPAP for the ongoing hypoxia, watching closely for any hemodynamic effect from the added intrathoracic pressure.
relatedChecklist: Norepinephrine infusion 1.7 mcg/min (85 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min), titrate to MAP 65 mmHg
Apply CPAP for persistent hypoxia only after adequate fluid resuscitation and pressor support are underway

scenarioEvents.name: Perfusion and oxygenation improve, transport continues
scenarioEvents.description: With combined fluid, pressor, and respiratory support, the patient's perfusion and oxygenation trend toward normal. The crew continues serial reassessment and maintains the CPAP seal throughout transport.
relatedChecklist: Reassess full vital signs and CPAP seal at least every 15 minutes en route

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP applied before adequate fluid resuscitation
scenarioEvents.description: CPAP is applied for the hypoxia before an adequate fluid bolus has been completed. The added positive intrathoracic pressure further reduces preload in this volume-depleted septic patient, worsening hypotension.
relatedChecklist: Recognize CPAP-related preload drop; complete fluid resuscitation and reconsider CPAP pressure/pause if hypotension worsens

checklist.title: Administer supplemental oxygen via non-rebreather targeting SpO2 94-98%
Establish IV access; begin 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus, pressure infused over less than 15 min toward MAP 65 mmHg
Norepinephrine infusion 1.7 mcg/min (85 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min), titrate to MAP 65 mmHg
Apply CPAP for persistent hypoxia only after adequate fluid resuscitation and pressor support are underway
Reassess full vital signs and CPAP seal at least every 15 minutes en route
Recognize CPAP-related preload drop; complete fluid resuscitation and reconsider CPAP pressure/pause if hypotension worsens
